hens_rule_text: The city's own Municipal Code Title 6 has a dedicated Chapter 6.05 titled FOWL, indicating chickens are regulated rather than banned, but the specific hen count cap could not be confirmed from available extracts.
permit_notes: No permit requirement was confirmed for the city (a different rule, requiring an accessory-use permit for some counts, applies to unincorporated San Bernardino County, a separate jurisdiction, and should not be read as the city's rule).
setback_notes: City Municipal Code Sec. 6.05.040 (Roosters and Peacocks Not Permitted Within 200 Feet of Human Dwelling) bans roosters and peacocks within 200 ft of any human dwelling; this is the only distance figure confirmed for the city chapter.
zoning_notes: Do not confuse the incorporated City of San Bernardino's Municipal Code (Title 6, Chapter 6.05 FOWL) with unincorporated San Bernardino County's separate Development Code (Title 8, Chapter 84.04 Animal Keeping); most search results returned the county rule, which does not apply inside city limits.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: San Bernardino, CA Code of Ordinances, Title 6 Animals, Chapter 6.05 Fowl (amlegal)
Sec. 6.05.040 Roosters and Peacocks Not Permitted Within 200 Feet of Human Dwelling (amlegal)

research_notes: codelibrary.amlegal.com is region-blocked from this machine for the city's own code (sanbernardinoca), and the individual chapter/section pages were not found in the Wayback Machine (only the Title-level table of contents page archived, which confirmed Chapter 6.05 FOWL exists and lists Sec. 6.05.040 by title). Most search-engine results conflate the incorporated city with unincorporated San Bernardino County's separate and more detailed Development Code, which quotes specific hen counts (e.g. 2 to 4 female poultry by lot size) that belong to the county, not the city; those numbers were deliberately excluded here. Max hens, permit requirement, and slaughter rules for the city itself remain unconfirmed.
